title: devbin's own release command acts on --help after its verb: release notes --help rewrites both views, release check --help runs the check
body:
Found by the research behind 0064's design on 2026-09-14, from reading `bin/.devbin/cmd/release`, and reproduced before filing -- in a throwaway clone of devbin at `7d70399`, never in this tree:

    $ printf 'MARKER-hand-edit\n' >>CHANGELOG.md
    $ grep -c MARKER-hand-edit CHANGELOG.md
    1
    $ ./bin/devbin release notes --help
    wrote CHANGELOG.md and RELEASES.md from RELEASES/ (2 release(s))
    $ echo $?
    0
    $ grep -c MARKER-hand-edit CHANGELOG.md
    0
    $ ./bin/devbin release check --help
    release views are current
    $ ./bin/devbin release --help
    usage: devbin release <notes|check>

The last command is the control: help asked for in the verb's position is answered. **The command reads only its first argument.** Its `case` answers `-h | --help` there and nowhere else, and the `notes` and `check` arms never look at what follows them, so asking a verb for help RUNS the verb.

## Why it is worth an issue when the write is a regeneration

The views are generated, so on a tree whose views are current the rewrite is byte-identical and nothing is lost. On a tree where somebody has hand-edited `CHANGELOG.md` -- the state `release check` exists to catch -- `--help` silently discards the edit and exits 0, and the person who typed it was asking what the command does.

**It is also the one shape 0064 says a release core must not have.** 0064 records `macos prepare --help` rebuilding and re-signing Intent.app on 2026-09-14 for exactly this reason (intent#0395), and states that `--help` never cuts a release. The same research read the same defect in Conflab's release command, where `release --patch --help` would cut a full release; that was read from source and not run, it is Conflab's, and it is not filed here. Devbin's own notes half has the defect, and the core will be built beside it.

## Shape of a fix, not a ruling

Read every argument before acting, as Intent's orchestrator does, so `--help` in any position prints usage and exits 0. Hold it with an arm per verb asserting that `<verb> --help` changes no file -- measured on the files' bytes rather than on the output, because `notes` prints the same `wrote` line whether or not it was asked for help.



## Fixed at `30b40ab`, by vc on 2026-09-16, in 0.1.1 on hv's instruction

`bin/.devbin/cmd/release` now reads every argument before a verb acts. `--help` in any position prints usage and exits 0. Any other word after `notes` or `check` is refused before anything is written, because neither verb takes one; `notes --dry-run` would otherwise have regenerated both views.

Three arms in `tests/unit/release.bats`, each measured on the views' bytes rather than on output, all red first: `notes --help` writes neither view and keeps a hand edit; `check --help` prints usage over stale views instead of reporting them; `notes --dry-run` refuses and writes nothing. Two mutations each turned exactly the expected arms red: help read only in the first position (arms 1 and 2), and no refusal of an extra argument (arm 3). `release.bats` 27 of 27; lint clean.

This is the `--help` shape 0064 says a release core must never have, so ST0007's design inherits the rule.
